text:
sam: Heads up — saw a 12-18% token-throughput regression on MQA paged-attn after yesterday's kernel-handoff change. Landing /hotfix reverted the selector but we still see variance.
amy: yikes. which config did the selector pick for the failing traces? architecture, blocksize, or seqlen path? :thinking:
sam: selector favoured the unified-gqa-path with kvcache interleaved layout for a bunch of 1-4 token short bursts. We expected MQA-specialized kernel but it chose GQA fallback.
jonathan: can you paste the perf samples? even a couple of traces will help.
sam: pasted short samples below — these are from a 512-batch synthetic replay hitting the live routing policy

# before (old selector): avg token/us = 0.85, p95 latency=22ms, kernel=MQA_paged_block16
# after (new selector):  avg token/us = 0.72, p95 latency=28ms, kernel=GQA_unified_block32
# KV-cache hit pattern: high fragmentation on per-shard prefix -> many small page reads

lucy: hmm fragmentation + wrong kernel pick. Selector scoring weight for `kvcache_fragmentation` was lowered in the diff? @jonathan did you touch that?
jonathan: I increased seqlen_bias to favor shorter paths (PR #4121) because we regressed on long-seq workloads. Looks like that unintentionally pulls traffic into unified path for MQA workloads with tiny seqlen distribution.
amy: can we reproduce on perf harness with mixed MQA/GQA traffic? I'll run replay with the exact prefix patterns.
perf-bot: scheduled perf replay job `replay-283333` -> status: running
sam: experiment notes: when kernel picks GQA_unified_block32 on paged-kv with fragmented cache, we pay extra page zeroing and more host->device copies.
jonathan: idea: add a fast gate that overrides unified pick when `kvcache_frag_score > 0.6 && mqa_capable == true` — basically a cost heuristic.
lucy: agree. also consider lowering the blocksize threshold: for paged-attn MQA path block16 tends to win on small page-read counts.
amy: I'll run three replays: (A) master with revert, (B) current selector, (C) selector + frag-gate. Compare tokens/us and page-read counts.
sam: quick sanity check: config snippet to try
```yaml
selector:
  seqlen_bias: 0.75
  frag_gate:
    enabled: true
    threshold: 0.6
  block_preference:
    mqa: [16, 24]
    gqa: [32, 48]
```
jonathan: implementation note: frag score is cheap to compute from active cache segments; add it to the per-request scoring in the fast path (avoid full profiler call).
amy: replay results (A/B/C) — preliminary numbers from my laptop harness (lower fidelity but directional):
- A (revert): avg token/us 0.86, page_reads_per_token 0.14
- B (current): avg token/us 0.71, page_reads_per_token 0.28
- C (frag-gate): avg token/us 0.84, page_reads_per_token 0.15
sam: C looks promising, matches prod delta. Any risk of oscillation if frag_score is noisy?
jonathan: add hysteresis: frag_gate only flips if score stays > threshold for N consecutive requests or over a short sliding window; also cap gate changes per-connection.
lucy: also log a tiny metric `selector.override.reason` with tags `{frag, seqlen, capacity}` so we can trace when the gate fires.
amy: sounds good. I'll push a branch with frag-gate + hysteresis + metric. Want reviewers: @sam @jonathan.
sam: thanks. follow-up actions:
- amy: push branch + perf replays by EOD
- jonathan: add frag_score into fast scorer + unit test
- lucy: add metric & dashboards for override counts
- sam: roll candidate to canary with 5% and watch token/us + page_reads
perf-bot: job `replay-283333` finished: summary -> master vs candidate C shows +18% tokens/us on mixed MQA workloads
jonathan: excellent. once we have unit tests and a small benchmark, I'll approve.
sam: minor note: add a debug log that prints `picked_kernel` and `frag_score` for the first N requests per trace so SRE can correlate without full traces.
lucy: ack. should we make the gate configurable per-customer (dedicated/private) to be safe?
amy: yes. implement default enabled=true for hosted, opt-in for dedicated until we validate.
sam: I'll schedule a short postmortem doc if anything slips during canary but looks like we have a low-risk plan. :thumbsup:
jonathan: thanks all — great catch. We'll iterate on thresholds after the canary metrics.
